sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the full length of the Gargano Promontory, and belongs to the oblique to right-lateral strike-slip system that affects the central and southern Adriatic foreland. This Source is the near-vertical, ca. N-dipping, Mattinata fault, well to the east of the main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a dense intermediate to damaging seismicity in and around this region. From west to east, the key earthquakes are: 6 December 1875 (Mw 6.1, S. Marco in Lamis) and 21 February 1841 (Mw 5.4, S. Marco in Lamis), 18 August 1948 (Mw 5.6, Puglia settentrionale), 8 December 1889 (Mw 5.5, Apricena), and the 19 June 1975 (Mw 5.0), 30 September 1995 (Mw 5.2), and 10 August 1893 (Mw 5.4) Gargano events.
This Source represents a deep E-W fault system that has been active as far back as the Mesozoic with various kinematics and controlled by shifting tectonic regimes through geologic time. Inherited and well developed structural patterns, in part abandoned and in part reactivated in the current stress regime, have left a dramatic landscape imprint in the outcropping Apulian platform. Such constraint have made the investigation of younger (and comparatively smaller) geologic features more difficult. Field evidence and recent seismological data have shed light on a complex structural arrangement made of (a) shallower (within the uppermost ca. 12 km) faults that affect the ground surface and that were associated to some historical earthquakes, and of (b) deeper (down to ca. 25 km) structures that may have caused the recent Mw ca. 5.0 instrumental events.
Three segments of this Source have been associated with key earthquakes that have affected this region. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Sources in this Database.
The strike of this source was based on that of the mapped structures. The dip was based on geological and seismological data. The rake represents oblique, right-lateral strike slip, based on geological and seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological and seismological data. The slip rate was based on geological data.

evidence: Inferred from lower depth of instrumental major earthquakes in the region.

pictures.t: Instrumental seismicity of the Mattinata fault zone
